source.title: Rep2Text: Decoding Full Text from a Single LLM Token Representation
source.authors: Haiyan Zhao; Zirui He; Yi-Ming Tang; Fan Yang; Ali Payani; Dian-Bo Liu; Meng-Nan Du

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some figures and extracted text are garbled, but the relevant tables and prose are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model transfer using a learned adapter and reconstruction metrics, rather than measuring representation-distance convergence.
record.gate_note: Only cross-model inversion results are linked to V4: the adapter maps a target model's last-token representation into a decoder's token-embedding space, and the paper compares self- and cross-model decoding. The paper does not measure representational similarity or distance alignment. Sequence-length, layer, training-data-size, and other inversion results do not test the listed claim versions. The Random and Reverse correspondence conditions test whether inversion relies on representation-specific information, not V4 transfer between models.
record.test_reason: Rep2Text trains a two-layer MLP adapter, on 640K pairs, that turns a target LLM's last-token state into soft-prompt embeddings for a decoder LLM. It then scores the reconstructed text. Even self-decoding (same model as target and decoder) goes through a trained adapter. So the self vs cross comparison shows which decoder reads the information equally well. It does not show that one model's representations map onto another's representation space with little loss. The mapping targets input token embeddings, not the other model's hidden states, and no loss relative to the original representation is measured. The cross-model mapping is the method's tool, and the results are the method's reconstruction performance. No version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misweighted. The main conclusion concerns invertibility: roughly half the tokens of 16-token inputs are recoverable from one last-token representation, with strong semantic preservation. Recovery falls with sequence length while topic persists, and the method transfers partly to out-of-distribution clinical data. Cross-model decoding being robust, and decoder family mattering more than scale, are secondary findings. The authors infer that recoverable information is 'partially aligned across different LLMs'. They also warn that intermediate representations pose a privacy risk.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a trained two-layer MLP adapter to project a target model's last-token state into decoder token embeddings, then measures reconstructed-text quality. It does not measure cross-model representational-distance similarity.
record.method_sensitivity: Decoder family and decoder size affect reconstruction scores; the authors report that decoder family matters more than scale.

fits_no_version.finding: At layer 10, a frozen Llama-3.1-8B decoder reconstructs Llama-3.2-3B last-token states about as well as the Llama-3.2-3B decoder (ROUGE-1 0.45 vs 0.46; BERTScore 0.76 vs 0.76). Each decoder gets its own trained adapter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information in one LLM's last-token state can be read out by a different LLM via a learned nonlinear adapter, about as well as by the same model.

fits_no_version.finding: For Mistral-7B layer-10 states, Llama decoders (3B, 8B) reach ROUGE-1 0.52. Qwen decoders reach 0.47–0.51, with no monotonic gain from 14B to 72B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model adapter readout depends on decoder family more than decoder scale.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (stated in the text); venue metadata also identifies arXiv.org.
record.problems: The cross-model result is based on a learned nonlinear adapter and text reconstruction, not direct measurement of representation-to-representation similarity. The study does not report multiple seeds or formal significance tests; the checklist says this is due to computational cost.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for sequence-length, layer-wise, data-scale, correspondence-control, Vec2Text, or OOD inversion outcomes: these do not measure a claim version's inter-model alignment or interchangeability.

untested.parts: No alignment measured as a function of model scale or capability.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal data.
No mapping of one model's representations onto another's representation space, and no measure of mapping loss. Linear maps, stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are all absent.
No alignment level, plateau, or cause analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V4. I unlinked them. The adapter maps into soft-prompt embeddings and is trained separately for each target–decoder pair, including the self pair. The 'little loss' comparison is therefore between decoders, not between mapped and original representations. The authors' 'partially aligned' remark is an interpretation, not a test. If curators read V4 broadly, r1–r4 would weakly support it and r5–r14 would limit its scope by decoder family.

versions.untested_parts: No test of representation alignment increasing with model scale or capability.
No vision-language paired-data or cross-modal alignment test.
No comparison of seeds, shared features, or subspaces across same-architecture networks.

Tests a trained nonlinear adapter from a target model's representation to a decoder's embedding space using text reconstruction; does not test linear maps, stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or direct mapped-representation fidelity.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
No comparison of representation-convergence metrics, their settings, or in/out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of whether shared data or objectives explain representation alignment, or of an alignment plateau.
